ecological_question: Does abrupt day-night turnover coincide with a distinct habitat-state transition propensity in co-occurring geese and ducks beyond the time-matched choice opportunity and a fitted time-invariant within-birdyear habitat preference?
original_article_novelty: Original paper already establishes circadian movement patterns and species-specific habitat functional responses; new endpoint is successive within-bird, across-photoperiod habitat-category transitions relative to independent-source availability baseline, NOT movement incidence or habitat preference.

hypotheses.primary: Within the same original bird-year, source season, prior habitat class, and arriving day/night photoperiod, observed habitat-category change residual beyond fitted static-preference opportunity is higher for an hourly transition crossing day/night than within the same photoperiod. Report all species, including negative or uncertain.
hypotheses.secondary: Direction of origin-category-to-destination-category moves between Rice and Protected may differ for night→day versus day→night, and may differ among species; no claim that the categories directly measure feeding/sanctuary use, and no multiple-testing rescue.

cohort.events: One source one-hot observed destination and source generated available-destination 7-category count vector for each birdyear/species/timestamp, with total 20–100; exact same source exclusions as source-verified California V2.
cohort.transition: Previous and next qualified events strictly 55–65 minutes apart, same source 'season' category. Crossing photoperiod defined only by source's day/night label. 9586 expected crossing transitions; no inferred sunrise or local clock.
cohort.individual: Source birdyear suffix _YYYY split into candidate tag for repeated-year blocking, consistent with prior ID audit. 254 candidate tag IDs expected across 329 bird-years.
cohort.study: One California telemetry study with four species, not four independent sample universes.

models.static_preference: Same original bird-year seven-class Dirichlet(0.5) count smoothing, IPF preference fitted to marginal observed source used-category frequencies and seven-category time-varying matched available destination counts, match each birdyear's broad marginal used/available state. No outcome-based change after ecological results.
models.residual: For a used previous category a and next category b, y=1[b!=a], expected switch probability 1-p_{t,a} from fitted independent static-preference time-matched choice, residual r = y - (1-p_t,a). No claim these independently chosen destinations preserve true space/route autocorrelation.
models.baseline: Within each individual birdyear × source season × current photoperiod × immediately previous habitat category, compute the difference in mean residual for boundary vs nonboundary hours; require >=2 transitions of each type and positive within-category comparison. Per candidate tagged ID, pool eligible strata by their equal-stratum mean (all accepted strata equal within tag) and require >=4 valid strata total and >=4 source boundary transitions. A bird's repeated year measurements do not count as additional independent IDs.
models.group_summary: One independent candidate tagged ID one vote, per-species mean primary boundary-excess-switch probability in percentage points, 10,000 seeded ID bootstrap 95% CI and count of IDs with positive contrasts. If fewer than 5 estimable individuals for a species report NOT_ESTIMABLE, do not borrow from other taxa.
models.noninference: No pooled multi-species p-value or statement about individual daytime feeding; preliminary post-result comparison is observational and circadian source label is not the precise astronomical dawn.

descriptive_secondary.source_transition_table: Counts and 10,000 tag-bootstrap CI for observed Rice→Protected and Protected→Rice as percentages of all category changes at day→night and night→day boundaries separately. Require >=15 independent IDs with at least one such source origin-state event to provide uncertainty intervals; else report counts with INSUFFICIENT_BRANCHES, no sign test or salvaged outcome.
descriptive_secondary.no_cherry_pick: Report all four species×two direction sets whether observed contrasts favor the candidate biological story or not.
descriptive_secondary.avoid_overclaim: Protected category is management status and Rice is crop land cover; neither directly certifies roost/feeding function or hunting refuge use at any source move.

limits: Source data retain moving-step endpoints, not the full stationary process and not origin habitat at the actual step start.
Day-night boundary movement within 55–65 minutes is not independent of original movement activity or route geography, so observed change does not prove active habitat switching due to light.
A fitted static preference reference is an imperfect spatial/behavioral null, not a structural availability or randomized environmental-change test.
The original authors studied circadian movement and habitat selection; novelty depends on temporal transitions not those already known behaviors.
Conditioning on source season and arrival photoperiod does not control the exact time of day, individual local neighborhood, geographical route or shared patch inertia.
All hypotheses frozen after original source selection and aggregate outcome examination; any test is explicitly exploratory.
positive_support_gate: Only a 95% candidate-ID bootstrap lower bound >0 within each species supports that exploratory species-specific increased boundary switching. Negative intervals reduce the comparative paper's generality claim rather than altering analysis thresholds.
